answer_plain: Four degrees of climate warming changes hydrogen uptake over two weeks by 7.2 % when rainfall stays the same (range -13 to 10 %), so uptake may go up or down depending on whether faster enzyme activity outweighs faster drying of the sand; warming the sand alone by ten degrees without extra drying changes uptake by 69 % (range 3.8 to 78 %).
answer_science: Central percentage change: h2_uptake_change_pct = 7.158 % (median -2.645 %, 50 % IQR [-7.688, 2.714] %, joint 5–95 % interval [-13.22, 9.975] %) (rounded headline: 7.2 %); absolute change h2_uptake_contrast_umol_m2 = 78.91 µmol m⁻² (median -15.44 µmol m⁻², 50 % IQR [-93.26, 13.64] µmol m⁻², joint 5–95 % interval [-380, 82.52] µmol m⁻²); absolute uptake h2_uptake_umol_m2 = 1181 µmol m⁻² (median 918.7 µmol m⁻², 50 % IQR [337, 2199] µmol m⁻², joint 5–95 % interval [125.2, 4530] µmol m⁻²) (mode = variance, refusal fraction = 0.0 %, max level refusal across question = 0.0 %). Top two Sobol' contributors to output variance: q10 (ST = 0.75 [0.69, 0.82], S1 = 0.71) and evap_scaling_per_c (ST = 0.15 [0.13, 0.16], S1 = 0.15). Status share of variance: verified_in_source ST = 0.15 (S1 = 0.15), modeller_assumption ST = 0.85 (S1 = 0.85), source_not_checked ST = 0.00 (S1 = 0.00) (joint group total indices can sum to more than 1 because of interactions). Limits: The parameter-uncertainty interval quantifies joint variation over literature constants and twin process parameters only and excludes external-model and twin model-structure error.

headline_plain: Four degrees of climate warming changes hydrogen uptake over two weeks by 7.2 %, and uptake may go up or down across uncertain model numbers.
headline_science: Central h2_uptake_change_pct = 7.158 % (median -2.645 %, 50 % IQR [-7.688, 2.714] %, joint 5–95 % interval [-13.22, 9.975] %) (plain headline: 7.2 %); absolute change h2_uptake_contrast_umol_m2 = 78.91 µmol m⁻² (median -15.44 µmol m⁻², 50 % IQR [-93.26, 13.64] µmol m⁻², joint 5–95 % interval [-380, 82.52] µmol m⁻²); absolute uptake h2_uptake_umol_m2 = 1181 µmol m⁻² (median 918.7 µmol m⁻², 50 % IQR [337, 2199] µmol m⁻², joint 5–95 % interval [125.2, 4530] µmol m⁻²) (mode = variance, refusal = 0.0 %).
limits_plain: The range shows how much the answer moves when uncertain numbers in the models are varied; the models themselves could also be wrong. Heat stress death at extreme afternoon surface temperatures is not included in the simple warming curve.
limits_science: The parameter-uncertainty interval quantifies joint variation over literature constants and twin process parameters only and excludes external-model and twin model-structure error. Uses a monotonic Q10 temperature response without high-temperature protein denaturation or diurnal surface-skin thermal gradients.

admissibility.scope: Joint parameter and literature-constant uncertainty only; excludes model-structure error.
